football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Rutgers, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 6.1 points, but not the full gap. Input warning: EdgeDesk’s published number sits 7.0 points from the middle of its own other models. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Maryland has the ball (big plays through the air): Maryland’s offense turns 6.5% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Rutgers’ defense gives up explosive gains on 11.1% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).

When Rutgers has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Rutgers’ offense averages 9.1 yards per pass attempt, and Maryland’s defense allows 7.9 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.5).
In his last two games (Nebraska and Ohio State), Washington averaged 4.6 yards per attempt, against 6.8 in his four games before that.
In his last two games (howard and Indiana), Lonergan averaged 10.4 yards per attempt, against 7.6 in his two games before that.
contradicting: When Maryland has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Maryland’s offense has allowed a sack on 2.5% of its dropbacks, and Rutgers’ defense sacks the quarterback on 5.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Maryland has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Maryland’s offense averages 4.1 yards per carry, and Rutgers’ defense allows 7.4 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Rutgers has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Rutgers’ offense has allowed a sack on 8.1% of its dropbacks, and Maryland’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Maryland’s run defense No. 63 nationally and Rutgers’ No. 138.

Dylan Lonergan has completed 51 of 92 passes (55.4%) for 775 yards, 8.4 yards per attempt, 7 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in four games for Rutgers, and has been sacked on 5 of 97 dropbacks.
AJ Surace has completed 33 of 53 passes (62.3%) for 475 yards, 9.0 yards per attempt, 6 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in four games for Rutgers, and has been sacked on 8 of 61 dropbacks.
